source_snapshot.criteria: Installation completes, the system works after reboot and event logs contain no unexplained error/fail/warning messages.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL recognizes media and target requirements but does not define signed image, exact RAID VD guard, driver/partition/boot policy or complete event triage.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly treats installation as multi-step and destructive, but its generic scripted-install concept lacks target and recovery controls.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Adds stable RAID VD identity, USB/KVM supervision, complete Windows Setup/System/Application and BMC evidence.
historical_reviews.related_cases: Row92 builds RAID arrays; this row assumes one approved healthy VD and installs Windows. Row94 updates its RAID driver/firmware separately.
historical_reviews.v3_1: A successful boot is insufficient without proof of the exact target, intended layout, supported RAID driver and unexplained-event disposition.

original_test_intent: Install the approved Windows Server GUI release from USB onto the designated RAID virtual disk, reboot into a workable system and verify no unexplained event-log errors, failures or warnings.
original_method: A qualified operator boots signed media through KVM, confirms the stable RAID VD and approved layout, supervises installation and one reboot, while the agent preserves full setup, storage, boot, event and BMC evidence.
manual_activity: User approves media, exact VD, data loss, layout and recovery; operator boots USB and supervises target selection/reboot; agent assists only with approved deployment and evidence.
required_inputs: Signed Windows Server GUI image/version/license and USB checksum
RAID controller/VD stable identity, capacity and all non-target exclusions
Supported RAID driver plus partition, format, boot, encryption and answer-file policy
Hostname/network/account secret policy and known-event allowlist
Backup image, KVM/OOB, maintenance window and boot/storage recovery
safety_requirements: Verify exact RAID VD identity/capacity at the installer and never use installer order alone
Confirm signed media and supported driver before formatting
Preserve pre-install storage/boot/BMC evidence and all Setup logs
Stop on target ambiguity, unexpected partitions, driver/media error, boot/storage/BMC fault or unexplained events
Do not auto-repartition, suppress events, repeatedly reboot or expose credentials
agent_execution_scope: Collect complete controller/VD/physical-disk and boot baseline
Validate media/driver and assist only with the approved attended or guarded unattended installation
After one reboot, collect OS/version, boot target, layout, driver/storage health and complete event logs
Do not choose target or destructive policy, operate unseen KVM steps or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Approve media, exact target/layout, known-event policy and recovery
Provide KVM/operator and own data-loss/boot recovery decisions
Review Setup, boot, storage and event evidence and decide PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The high-level scripted-install suggestion is directionally valid but lacks a guarded target selector, signed media/driver validation, reboot proof and complete event-log acceptance.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the approved Windows installer/answer file only after stable RAID VD confirmation, capture full Setup logs, then collect boot configuration, disk/driver state and complete System/Application/Setup events after one controlled reboot.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: USB boot, Windows Server GUI installation, reboot/workability, event-log review and source 10/20 timing fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Perform a target-guarded signed-media deployment with operator confirmation at destructive boundaries and a complete post-reboot event/storage acceptance bundle.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact identity, data protection, driver support and event-triage traceability without reducing installation scope.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Automation may assist installation but cannot silently choose the VD or replace KVM/USB and engineer event disposition.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Installer disk numbering can differ from controller VD numbering, so model/capacity alone may be insufficient; controller and installer identities must be reconciled.

project_override_considerations: Known Windows warnings are acceptable only when individually approved with source/build applicability; a blanket warning exclusion is not valid.
expected_evidence: Approval, license and signed media/driver checksums
Pre/post controller VD and physical-drive maps plus exact selected target
Partition/format/encryption/boot configuration and full Windows Setup logs
Windows version, active boot/root volume, RAID driver/storage health and complete System/Application/Setup plus BMC/SEL logs
Known-event triage, backup/recovery and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Master Procedure and Criteria consistently define Windows installation, reboot and event review; the reference reviews differ only in completeness.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Media, target, driver, KVM and recovery are supplyable execution prerequisites; the static review is complete.

review_improvement: Makes the destructive target and full post-reboot event/storage acceptance auditable instead of treating generic deployment or boot success as sufficient.
independent_technical_reasoning: Windows Setup can renumber disks and load a RAID driver that exposes several similar VDs, so target selection must reconcile controller and installer identity before formatting. A workable desktop also does not prove clean deployment: Setup, System and Application logs plus boot/storage state must be reviewed against a narrow approved known-event list.
